56425-the-mountain-of-fears.title: The Mountain Of Fears
56425-the-mountain-of-fears.creator: Unknown
56425-the-mountain-of-fears.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Leyden leaned both elbows on the taffrail and listened restlessly. Our little ship swashed through the short sling of the Spanish Main, the Pole star gleaming ahead, the Southern Cross blazing astern, and all about the white, flashing crests of the phosphorescent sea. Usually Leyden was a good listener, but this night he seemed impatient, restive, to such an extent that I finally paused, annoyed, for nothing is so irritating as lack of attention to a solicited reply.

arxiv-2307-16809.title: An Enhanced System for the Detection and Active Cancellation of Snoring Signals
arxiv-2307-16809.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . Snoring is a common disorder that affects people’s social and marital lives. The annoyance caused by snoring can be partially solved with active noise control systems. In this context, the present work aims at introducing an enhanced system based on the use of a convolutional recurrent neural network for snoring activity detection and a delayless subband approach for active snoring cancellation.

arxiv-2309-05911.title: Quality-Agnostic Deepfake Detection with Intra-model Collaborative Learning
arxiv-2309-05911.creator: Binh M. Le, Simon S. Woo
arxiv-2309-05911.description: Abstract Deepfake has recently raised a plethora of societal concerns over its possible security threats and dissemination of fake information. Much research on deepfake detection has been undertaken. However, detecting low quality as well as simultaneously detecting different qualities of deepfakes still remains a grave challenge.

arxiv-2412-17696.title: Understanding the Logic of Direct Preference Alignment through Logic
arxiv-2412-17696.creator: Kyle Richardson, Vivek Srikumar, Ashish Sabharwal
arxiv-2412-17696.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kyle Richardson, Vivek Srikumar, Ashish Sabharwal. Recent direct preference alignment algorithms (DPA), such as DPO , have shown great promise in aligning large language models to human preferences. While this has motivated the development of many new variants of the original DPO loss, understanding the differences between these recent proposals, as well as developing new DPA loss functions, remains difficult given the lack of a technical and conceptual framework for reasoning about the underlying semantics of these algorithms.

arxiv-2602-09904.title: Safeguarding Privacy: Privacy-Preserving Detection of Mind Wandering and Disengagement Using Federated Learning in Online Education A Preprint
arxiv-2602-09904.creator: Anna Bodonhelyi, Mengdi Wang, Efe Bozkir, Babette Bühler, Enkelejda Kasneci
arxiv-2602-09904.description: Abstract Since the COVID-19 pandemic, online courses have expanded access to education, yet the absence of direct instructor support challenges learners’ ability to self-regulate attention and engagement. Mind wandering and disengagement can be detrimental to learning outcomes, making their automated detection via video-based indicators a promising approach for real-time learner support.

pmc-10625544.title: Glutamate secretion by embryonic stem cells as an autocrine signal to promote proliferation
pmc-10625544.creator: Lin Teng, Qin Qin, Ziyi Zhou, Fei Zhou, Chunyu Cao, Jian Yang, Jiawang Ding
pmc-10625544.description: Glutamate, the major excitatory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system, has also been found to play a role in embryonic stem (ES) cells. However, the exact mechanism and function of glutamatergic signaling in ES cells remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified a glutamatergic transmission circuit in ES cells that operates through an autocrine mechanism and regulates cell proliferation.

pmc-11290237.title: Link between bacterial communities and contrasted loads in ectoparasitic monogeneans from the external mucus of two wild sparid species (Teleostei)
pmc-11290237.creator: Judith Revault, Yves Desdevises, Élodie Magnanou
pmc-11290237.description: BackgroundWhile teleost fishes represent two thirds of marine vertebrates, the role of their external microbiota in relationship with their environment remains poorly studied, especially in wild populations. Hence, the interaction of their microbiota with ectoparasites is largely unknown. Microbiota can act as a protective barrier against pathogens, and/or be involved in host recognition by parasites.

pmc-11528165.title: Phenotyping Adherence Through Technology-Enabled Reports and Navigation (the PATTERN Study): Qualitative Study for Intervention Adaptation Using the Exploration, Preparation, Implementation, and Sustainment Framework
pmc-11528165.creator: Allison P Pack, Stacy C Bailey, Rachel O'Conor, Evelyn Velazquez, Guisselle Wismer, Fangyu Yeh, Laura M Curtis, Kenya Alcantara, Michael S Wolf, Amaryllis Mavragani, Heather Schacht Reisinger, Jeannys Nnemnbeng
pmc-11528165.description: BackgroundOlder adults with multiple chronic conditions (MCC) and polypharmacy often face challenges with medication adherence. Nonadherence can lead to suboptimal treatment outcomes, adverse drug events, and poor quality of life.ObjectiveTo facilitate medication adherence among older adults with MCC and polypharmacy in primary care, we are adapting a technology-enabled intervention previously implemented in a specialty clinic.

pmc-11570458.title: Evaluation of the phytochemical, bioactive compounds and descriptive sensory of encapsulated lingzhi (Ganoderma lucidum) extracts with combined wall materials for masking effect on the perception of off-flavour and bitterness

However, its use is limited due to factors such as bitterness, flavour, and astringency.

pmc-12500924.title: Four decades of annual monitoring reveal declining reproductive success of a migratory baleen whale
pmc-12500924.creator: Els Vermeulen, Christopher Wilkinson, Peter B. Best, Ken Findlay
pmc-12500924.description: Understanding and mitigating threats to species survival relies on the ability to track key demographic processes over time. Among these processes, reproduction stands out as a primary biological driver of population growth and resilience. Multiple factors affect reproductive success, including environmental variables and resource availability.

pmc-13168220.title: Unraveling genetic diversity in ‘Foşa’ and ‘Yomra’ hazelnut accessions (Corylus avellana L.) using SSR markers and phenotypic analysis
pmc-13168220.creator: Yusuf Bilgen, Yaşar Akça, Kenan Yıldız, Kubilay Yıldırım
pmc-13168220.description: The Foşa hazelnut variety is commonly cultivated in Türkiye and is often confused with the Yomra variety due to morphological similarities. This study aims to determine the phenological and pomological characteristics of the Foşa and Yomra hazelnut populations and reveal their genetic diversity using multivariate statistical analysis and Simple Sequence Repeat (SSR) molecular markers.

pmc-13409244.title: Psychology of Eating the Future: Consumer Acceptance, Digital Influence and Behavioral Drivers of Novel Foods
pmc-13409244.creator: Muhammad Faisal Manzoor, Muhammad Talha Afraz, Muhammad Waseem, Zahoor Ahmed
pmc-13409244.description: The accelerating urgency of global public health challenges, biodiversity loss, and climate change has driven rapid innovation in novel foods and alternative proteins, including cultured cells, fermentation-derived components, plant-based meats, insects, and algae, which promise nutritious, sustainable, and ethical dietary choices with lower environmental footprints.

pmc-13470271.title: Natufian sickle blades (ca. 15,000–11,700 cal. BP) reveal cereal cultivation ca. 4.5 millennia before domestication
pmc-13470271.creator: Iris Groman-Yaroslavski, Tamar Krugman, Anna Belfer-Cohen, Reuven Yeshurun, Leore Grosman, Daniel Kaufman, Katerina Barshay, Maria Piliponsky, Jacob Vardi, Itay Abadi, Mina Weinstein-Evron
pmc-13470271.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study reveals a hitherto undocumented cereal procurement strategy employed during the Late Epipaleolithic Natufian culture of the Southern Levant, from ca. 4.5 to 1 millennia before systematic crop cultivation and domestication are identified in archaeological records. A comprehensive microscopic use-wear analysis of flint sickle blades from the sites of el-Wad Terrace and Salibiya I detected patterns generated by the harvest of semi-ripe and ripe cereals that are attributed to the shattering mechanism of cereals.

pmc-13514021.title: Prevalence of nicotine, alcohol, and cannabis use disorders among adults with chronic pain: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13514021.creator: Andrew H. Rogers, Emily L. Zale, Jessica M. Powers, Yohannes W. Woldeamanuel, Nell Aronoff, Laurel Mueller, Chung Jung Mun, Marianna Mazza, Marianna Mazza, Marianna Mazza, Marianna Mazza
pmc-13514021.description: Chronic pain is a significant public health problem associated with substantial medical expenditures, decreased quality of life, and physical and mental health comorbidities. Substance use is an important clinical consideration in pain, as substance use has been identified as both an antecedent and consequence of chronic pain.

pmc-13594663.title: Motor cortex rTMS modulates adult ocular dominance plasticity
pmc-13594663.creator: İzel D Sarı, Vasileia Papakosta, Xavier Corominas Teruel, Hanna Willis, Antoni Valero-Cabré, Claudia Lunghi
pmc-13594663.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Well-established evidence supports cross-modal interactions of sensory brain plasticity. Here, we extend cross-modality beyond the boundaries of sensory regions and provide first-time evidence in adult healthy humans that motor plasticity influences homeostatic visual plasticity. To this end, we employed repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), known to modulate the excitation/inhibition balance in the primary motor cortex (M1), while examining the impact of this intervention on ocular dominance plasticity induced by short-term monocular deprivation (MD).

pmc-13681079.title: Therapeutic efficacy of mesenchymal stem cells in periodontal regeneration: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials
pmc-13681079.creator: Fiki Muhammad Ridho, Anis Irmawati, Raed Labib, Hayyu Norma Almira, Ridwan Alfatah, Bayu Cahyo Bintoro
pmc-13681079.description: BackgroundPeriodontitis is a major global health problem that leads to destruction and loss of periodontal tissues. As conventional therapy has a limited capacity to restore the complex architecture of the periodontium, regenerative approaches have been explored. This meta-analysis evaluates the therapeutic efficacy of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) for periodontal regeneration in patients with periodontal defects.
